additional_requirements: manic_episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the active and residual portions of the illness
delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S021.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
S021.description: Symptoms where speech or thought appears scattered and difficult to follow due to a lack of logical or consistent flow.

subtypes.Derailment or Loose Associations: A speech pattern of switching rapidly from one topic to another with no logical connection between thoughts.
subtypes.Tangentiality: Speech that deviates entirely from the question and fails to answer directly.
subtypes.Incoherence or Word Salad: Severe fragmentation of speech and sentence structure, making it nearly impossible to understand.
subtypes.Neologisms: Using made-up words that have meaning only to the individual.
subtypes.Clang Associations: Speech governed by sounds, such as rhyming, rather than the meaning of words.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.

subtypes.Responsiveness to Extraneous Stimuli: Attention is immediately drawn to trivial and unimportant stimuli nearby (e.g., noise, movement).
subtypes.Frequent Task Switching: Unable to finish one task and constantly shifting attention to new things, starting multiple tasks simultaneously.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Unable to focus on any activity for long, with attention constantly being scattered.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

S041.name: Painful_Consequence_Behavior
S041.description: Excessive involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences.

subtypes.Unrestrained Buying Sprees: Spending excessive amounts of money or shopping recklessly to a degree that creates financial distress for self and family.
subtypes.Foolish Business Investments: Making rash business investments or ventures without sufficient review.
subtypes.Sexual Indiscretions: Engaging in indiscriminate or risky sexual behavior that is out of character.
subtypes.Impulsive Risky Behavior: Excessively dangerous or foolish behavior, such as reckless driving or drug use, without considering the consequences.

info.persona: Angelica Beale navigates life with a disciplined curiosity, turning every gallery opening, garden harvest, and community photo shoot into a chance to weave cultural stories while stubbornly refusing to miss a weekly yoga class—even when the cold New York winter arrives, and they relish the rhythm of merengue evenings as a joyful release.
info.professional_persona: Angelica Beale, a seasoned curatorial specialist and museum docent, blends meticulous budget oversight, bilingual public outreach, and award‑winning grant writing with a disciplined drive to secure board membership and launch a mentorship pipeline for Caribbean‑heritage youth, and they approach every project with a curator’s eye for narrative cohesion.
info.cultural_background: Angelica is a first-generation Dominican-American. Her parents emigrated from the Dominican Republic in the early 1970s, and she grew up speaking Spanish at home while attending public schools in the Bronx. The rhythms of merengue and bachata, the flavors of mangú and sancocho, and the close-knit community celebrations of Dominican holidays have shaped her identity. After moving to Rockland County, she remained actively involved in local Dominican cultural organizations, participating in Independence Day parades, supporting Spanish-language literacy programs, and preserving family stories through oral history projects. Her bicultural experience informs her artistic sensibility, allowing her to blend Caribbean traditions with contemporary New York influences.
info.hobbies_and_interests: She spends her free time painting acrylics, exploring new art techniques, and attending gallery openings in NYC. Angelica is an avid reader of Latin American literature and writes book reviews for a local literary club. She enjoys cooking traditional Dominican dishes, dancing to merengue and bachata with friends, and maintaining a small herb garden. Weekly yoga and hikes in the Hudson Valley keep her active. She also pursues photography, documenting community events, and volunteers as a docent at a nearby museum, leading tours that highlight Caribbean contributions to American art.
info.sports_persona: Angelica Beale stays active through weekly yoga sessions, Saturday hikes with the Hudson Valley Hiking Club, and spirited support for the New York Knicks and Giants, preferring low‑impact endurance over competitive sports while they occasionally join community fun‑runs for a dash of excitement.
info.arts_persona: Angelica Beale, an avid acrylic painter, channels a curiosity for color akin to Frida Kahlo's bold palettes, curates exhibitions influenced by Basquiat's dynamic narratives, discerns literary nuance in works by Gabriel García Márquez, and they document community festivals through a Leica camera while serving as a docent championing Caribbean art.
info.travel_persona: Angelica Beale favors meticulously planned cultural getaways, alternating between weekend retreats to the Hudson Valley’s artisanal farms and longer voyages to historic art hubs like Barcelona and Cartagena, balancing a modest travel budget with a penchant for immersive museum tours, and they often map each itinerary with careful detail to ensure ample time for local art scenes.
info.culinary_persona: Angelica Beale, an adept home chef, frequently crafts aromatic island‑inspired meals such as plantain mofongo, cilantro‑lime grilled fish, and slow‑cooked yucca stew using herbs from their rooftop garden, while they occasionally indulge in a tasting menu at NYC’s Eleven Madison Park for inspiration.

info.persona: Demetrios Gomez is a calm, competitive thinker who blends bookkeeping precision with artistic curiosity, hiking trails and sketchbooks in hand, while they quietly master personal finance and indulge in indie‑rock soundtracks.
info.professional_persona: Demetrios Gomez is a meticulous junior accountant in the making, leveraging QuickBooks, Xero, and advanced Excel to turn numbers into clear visual insights while channeling a competitive curiosity into process‑automation projects that set the stage for a future CPA and boutique practice serving creative professionals.
info.cultural_background: Demetrios comes from a mixed Greek and Mexican heritage. His father, a second‑generation Greek‑American, introduced him to traditions such as Greek Easter, souvlaki, and Greek language phrases, while his mother’s Mexican‑American family celebrated Dia de los Muertos, shared salsa rhythms, and used Spanish expressions at home. Growing up in Coeur d’Alene, Idaho, he experienced a predominantly white community but retained a strong appreciation for his dual cultural roots, often blending Mediterranean and Latin American flavors in his cooking and enjoying folk music from both cultures. This multicultural background fuels his curiosity about art and new ideas, while the outdoors‑oriented lifestyle of the Pacific Northwest shaped his love for solitary exploration and resilience.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Demetrios enjoys solitary and small‑group activities that feed his curiosity and artistic side. He hikes the trails around Lake Coeur d’Alene, often photographing landscapes and sketching scenes in a small notebook. He frequents the local art gallery and experiments with watercolour painting and digital illustration, sometimes using his visual‑data skills to create infographics. Chess is a favorite pastime, allowing him to exercise his strategic mind. He reads non‑fiction books on philosophy, economics, and emerging technologies, and curates indie‑rock playlists. Occasionally, he joins a close‑knit group of friends for board‑game nights or tabletop role‑playing sessions.
info.sports_persona: Demetrios Gomez fuels a love for the outdoors with regular hikes around Lake Coeur d’Alene and spring trail runs with the Coeur d’Alene Trail Runners Club, follows the Seattle Seahawks in football, supports the Seattle Mariners in baseball, and winters snowboards at nearby Schweitzer Mountain, balancing solitary exertion with occasional pickup basketball at the local gym.
info.arts_persona: Demetrios Gomez regularly sketches watercolour landscapes in a pocket notebook, creates digital illustrations inspired by artists like James White and classic painters such as Claude Monet, curates indie‑rock playlists featuring Fleet Foxes, Tame Impala, and The National, and spends Friday evenings at the Coeur d’Alene Art Museum attending openings of emerging local artists.
info.travel_persona: Demetrios Gomez prefers meticulously planned solo or small‑group trips, having explored the Canadian Rockies, hiked in Glacier National Park, taken weekend road trips to Seattle and Spokane, and dreaming of a cultural immersion in Kyoto, Japan, all while keeping travel costs low through budget accommodations and early‑bird flight deals.
info.culinary_persona: Demetrios Gomez enjoys cooking at an intermediate level, often preparing grilled trout with fresh dill and lemon, a quinoa‑avocado salad dressed with olive oil and balsamic, and occasional homemade ramen featuring miso broth, soy sauce, and soft‑boiled eggs, showing a palate that balances healthy Pacific Northwest fare with bold Asian flavors.

info.persona: Nicole Johnson is a structured, goal‑driven 32‑year‑old who balances a rigorous warehouse routine with backyard gardening, weekend boxing, soulful music, and a penchant for Southern‑New Mexican fusion cooking, all while vigilantly managing a tight budget and occasionally letting a competitive streak eclipse collaborative moments.
info.professional_persona: Nicole Johnson is a reliable warehouse material mover whose meticulous safety focus, forklift mastery, and data‑driven inventory sequencing have made them the go‑to troubleshooter for bottlenecks and a natural candidate for shift‑supervisor promotion.
info.cultural_background: Nicole was raised in a close‑knit African‑American family that settled in Clovis, New Mexico, after her parents moved from Texas seeking steady work. Her upbringing blended the rich traditions of Black church life—spirituals, gospel choirs, and communal support—with the wide‑open landscapes and culinary influences of the Southwest. Family gatherings often feature collard greens seasoned with local chilies, and storytelling emphasizes perseverance and collective achievement. Nicole’s cultural identity is shaped by a strong sense of community, respect for elders, and an appreciation for both her African‑American heritage and the regional customs of New Mexico.
info.hobbies_and_interests: When she’s not on the warehouse floor, Nicole enjoys gardening in her backyard, where the predictable cycles of planting and harvesting provide a soothing contrast to the fast‑paced work environment. She loves cooking traditional Southern comfort foods with a New Mexican twist, often gathering family and church friends for potluck meals. Music is a constant companion—R&B, soul, and gospel tunes fill her home and accompany her weekend boxing classes, a hobby that satisfies her competitive spirit. Nicole also volunteers at her local church, helping organize community events, and she reads personal‑development books that reinforce her resilience and goal‑focused mindset.
info.sports_persona: Nicole Johnson trains at a neighborhood boxing club three evenings a week, follows the NFL's New Orleans Saints, supports the MLB's Houston Astros, and participates in monthly community 5K runs to stay fit, but they fiercely guard their win‑or‑lose mentality on the heavy bag.
info.arts_persona: Nicole Johnson fills their home with the soulful sounds of Aretha Franklin, Marvin Gaye, and contemporary gospel artist Tasha Cobbs, enjoys Sunday gospel choir performances at the local church, and when off‑beat, re‑watches classic films starring Denzel Washington, using music and film as both motivation for their workouts and comfort after a long shift.
info.travel_persona: Nicole Johnson prefers well‑planned road trips that combine horticulture inspiration and family time, having explored the historic gardens of Charleston, the adobe architecture of Santa Fe, and a weekend wine‑tasting retreat in Napa Valley, yet they keep a modest travel budget that prioritizes short stays over exotic adventures.
info.culinary_persona: Nicole Johnson cooks Southern comfort staples like chicken‑and‑dumplings, shrimp and grits, and sweet‑potato pie, but adds a New Mexican twist with roasted green chilies, red‑pepper salsa, and cumin, boasting an intermediate culinary skill set that lets them host regular potlucks for church friends while never quite mastering the perfect caramelized crust.
